title: Policy explainability: attach decision traces to audit logs and KMS tagging
author: Marin Okafor
description: Motivation: customers and internal auditors requested better visibility into why RBAC v2 decisions occur (especially around fallback/residency routing and KMS selection). Current audit envelopes record the decision outcome but not the decision trace. This PR attaches a compact, bounded "decision_trace" to audit logs and surfaces a KMS-tag header for downstream key usage attribution. Design summary: 1) Add a policy explainability layer that records the sequence of rule evaluations (rule id, short reason token, matched attributes) and a final score for the decision. The trace is canonicalized and truncated at 1KB to preserve audit throughput and avoid PII leakage. 2) Emit a new field in the audit envelope: decision_trace (compact JSON string). 3) Add a new outgoing header X-Redwood-KMS-Usage-Tag with a stable short tag derived from the decision (used for alignment with KMS billing/telemetry). 4) Integrate with RBAC v2 decision cache: cache now stores an optional explainability fingerprint and TTL; cache misses include the trace and are recorded in a metrics histogram. 5) Provide an opt-in org-level flag (policy_explainability.enabled) default=false; rollout plan below. Checklist implemented: - [x] Add explainability protobufs and serialization helpers - [x] Audit envelope schema migration with backward compatibility (old consumers ignore unknown fields) - [x] Truncation and scrubbers for attribute values (PII filter whitelist) - [x] Unit + integration tests for tracer and kernel path - [x] E2E test for KMS tag propagation to the kms-allocator and audit-forwarder - [x] Feature flag gating and gradual rollout config - [x] Docs for API and audit schema change (console + docs site) Key implementation notes: - The decision_trace is a compact array of tuples: ["rule_id","outcome","short_reason"]. We serialize to a base64-encoded compact JSON string to avoid breaking existing log parsers; consumers can opt to decode. Example (conceptual): {"decision_trace":"W1sicm9sZV8xIiwiYXQiLCJhdHRyaWJ1dGVfbWF0Y2gifSxbInJvbGVfMiIsIm5vIiwiZmFsbGJhY2siXQ=="} - Small snippet of change (rbac evaluator): "- decision := EvaluatePolicy(ctx, req)\n+ decision, trace := EvaluatePolicyWithTrace(ctx, req)\n+ EmitDecisionTrace(decision, trace)" Rollout and safety: - Feature is opt-in per-tenant; default off to avoid unexpected audit size increases. - We add a hard 1KB ceiling and safe scrubber: any attribute values matching PII patterns (emails, credit card-like numbers) are replaced with "<REDACTED>". - A new metric rbac.explainability.traces_emitted and rbac.explainability.truncations tracks usage and truncation rate. - For Dedicated/Private deployments we add an operator toggle in console; migration docs included. Backwards compatibility: audit-forwarder ignores unknown fields; the KMS allocator reads X-Redwood-KMS-Usage-Tag but falls back to existing heuristics if absent. Security review notes: scrubber whitelist reviewed by security; the trace only stores attribute keys (not raw user-provided text) except for enumerations and short tokens. Related work: ENG-4521 (policy observability), SEC-218 (KMS attribution). Linear links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4521/policy-explainability Implementation constraints and deliberate choices: - We avoid sending full policy ASTs to logs to reduce surface area. - The KMS tag is intentionally non-PII and reversible only with internal tooling. - Decision trace is not sent to external SaaS telemetry by default (flagged in telemetry pipeline). Migration notes: - Audit schema bump is backwards compatible; any consumer that does schema validation must pull the new schema v2.1. - Added migration guide in docs/redwood/audit/traces.md Testing: - Unit tests cover trace canonicalization and redaction rules. - Integration tests run in CI using a small policy set (tests/policy_explainability/*). - Ran local canary in staging for 72h (no perf regression: p50 +2ms, p99 +7ms on heavy auth paths). Performance: instrumentation shows median auth latency increase of ~1.9ms (trace disabled adds ~0.1ms); we added sampling and batching at 1000 TPS capacity. Link to full design doc: https://redwood.company/docs/design/policy-explainability

review_comments: Evelyn Chen (reviewer): Can we guarantee the trace size under adversarial inputs? Please add a hard truncation and a test — addressed in scrubber.go with 1KB cap (author)
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Is there any chance of exposing PII through attribute values? Please enumerate the scrub whitelist — added a whitelist and CI lint that flags missing entries (author)

Sofia Martinez (reviewer): KMS tag collision risk? How many bits of entropy are in the tag? — We use a 64-bit stable fingerprint salted per-tenant; added doc section and a test for collision rates (author)
Evelyn Chen (approval): Approving after the scrub tests and metric hooks were added. Small perf note addressed in follow-up (merge)
release_notes: Added opt-in per-tenant policy explainability traces attached to audit envelopes and a KMS usage tag header (X-Redwood-KMS-Usage-Tag). Default disabled. Includes scrubbers and truncation to limit audit size. See docs/audit/traces.md for migration steps and operator toggle instructions.
